# 2 Clement — Chapter 2 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 2
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. The scripture says: "Rejoice, O barren woman who bears no children! Shout for joy, you who never went into labor! For the desolate woman has more children than the one who has a husband." — When it says "Rejoice, O barren woman," it is speaking about us. Our church was barren — it had no children — until God gave them to it.
2. And "Shout for joy, you who never labored" — this means we should bring our prayers to God wholeheartedly, without losing heart the way a woman in labor does.
3. "The desolate woman has more children than the one with a husband" — this refers to the fact that our people once seemed abandoned by God. But now, because we believed, we have grown to outnumber those who always seemed to belong to God.
4. Another scripture puts it this way: "I did not come to call the righteous — I came to call sinners." The point is that the lost must be saved.
5. It is a remarkable and wonderful thing to strengthen those who are falling, not just those who are already standing firm.
6. That is exactly why Christ willed to save those who were going under — and he did save many of them, coming to call us when we were already perishing.
